newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Shots fired in Belgrade scuffle, arrests reported.
newsitem.headline: Shots fired in Belgrade scuffle, arrests reported.

text.p: Shots were fired in downtown Belgrade on Tuesday but no-one was injured in a scuffle between drunken youths and a motorist, witnesses said.
They said the incident, which occurred after dark, appeared to have nothing to do with an afternoon rally by 80,000 opposition supporters at the same downtown square.

"Dozens of youngsters were drinking brandy in front of the police," said one witness. "Later, when the police had left, they threw stones and pretended to be traffic police. When one car refused to stop, the hooligans broke its rear window. They were clearly drunk."

The driver jumped out and the youths started beating him. Someone fired several shots into the air with a pistol, witnesses said. The youths also forcibly stopped a city trolley bus, and someone got out and fired a warning shot.
Another witness said police arrived at the scene and arrested two youths.

For 77 days, opposition supporters and students have held largely peaceful demonstrations in Belgrade demanding that Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic reinstate opposition victories in lkocal elections last November 17.
